references.text: The preceding verse urges striving to enter through the narrow door, which forms the immediate context for the warning in verse 25 that the door will be shut ([ref:Luk 13:24|Luke 13:24]).

In the parable of the ten virgins, the door is also shut; those who arrive late knock and ask to be let in, but are told: "I do not know you" – a very close parallel to Luke 13:25 ([ref:Matt 25:10-12|Matthew 25:10-12]).

Jesus warns that many will say "Lord, Lord" on that day, but he will reply that he never knew them. This reflects the rejection in Luke 13:25 where the master of the house says "I do not know where you come from" ([ref:Matt 7:21-23|Matthew 7:21-23]).
Jesus asks why they call him "Lord, Lord" without doing what he says – a warning that reinforces the theme that it is not enough to invoke the Lord without true obedience ([ref:Luk 6:46|Luke 6:46]).

The entire parable of the ten virgins is about readiness and the risk of being shut out when the bridegroom arrives, which thematically closely resembles the warning in Luke 13:25 ([ref:Matt 25:1-13|Matthew 25:1-13]).
God shut the door to the ark after Noah and the others had entered – a picture that the door of grace is closed and it is no longer possible to enter ([ref:1 Mos 7:16|Genesis 7:16]).

Wisdom warns that those who reject her call will cry out without being heard when disaster comes – a theme of missed opportunity reflected in the shut door in Luke 13:25 ([ref:Ordsp 1:24-28|Proverbs 1:24-28]).

"Seek the Lord while he may be found, call on him while he is near" – a reminder that the opportunity to seek God is limited, just as Luke 13:25 shows that one day the door will be shut ([ref:Jes 55:6|Isaiah 55:6]).
The continuation of Jesus' speech where those rejected claim fellowship with him, but he repeats the rejection and calls them "workers of lawlessness" ([ref:Luk 13:26-27|Luke 13:26-27]).

Christ holds the key and opens and shuts, and no one can change it – a picture of his sovereign authority over access, corresponding to the master of the house who shuts the door in Luke 13:25 ([ref:Åp 3:7-8|Revelation 3:7-8]).

Esau found no opportunity for repentance even though he sought it with tears – a warning that it may become too late, parallel to those who knock in vain on the shut door ([ref:Hebr 12:16-17|Hebrews 12:16-17]).
